ops.title: Dispatch bursts unproven; sidechain prepare cost is path resolution, not listing
ops.body:
Milestone 2 findings for lane snapshot-oversize-clip (Nov 6, 2:55 PM PT). Full evidence: /Users/yasyf/.vcache/scratch/snapshot-oversize-clip/result-A.md (codex sol diagnosis, replay script scripts/replay_A.py) and result-B.md (Opus measurement, work/breakdown.py).

A, what serializes a long session's dispatch bursts: unproven. Real owner-global waits exist: the Go host owner admission (four hook slots, queue capped at 64) and the Rust prepared-fact read gate (claim_fact_read on one fact_read_in_flight flag; a blocked request can burn its deadline having read zero bytes). Neither is measured for dispatch 3089. Request 3c16...-10 spent its 731.8 ms inside the owner call (owner reported cancelled at 835.8 ms with 0 bytes read). Confirmed waste: every retain() creates a fresh Lease with an empty scalar memo, so sibling forks and concurrent clients recompute the same predicate (replay: 4 clients, 1 predicate, 32 query RPCs, 31 duplicates). The 0.75 s foreground deadline is one budget from the client's first snapshot call, so Python work before an RPC spends it (parent 3091: about 745 ms gone before its transport timer started). Missing evidence: per-parent RPC count and a timing split at worker exchange, Go slot admission, Rust dequeue, state mutex and fact-read gate.

B, sidechain listing: the listing is 0.37 ms of the 23 ms at 356 sidechains. Per-sidechain full-path resolution is 5.6 ms, the per-sidechain nested agent-<id>/subagents check is 4.7 ms (it never finds anything across 48,966 sidechains on this Mac), and size/mtime reads are 0.5 ms. A prepared graph stamps every sidechain and its first query fails changed if one moved, so under the current contract each prepare reads every sidechain once. The root names only 211 of 356 sidechains; 145 are named only by their parent sidechain once they finish. Options: 1 cache resolved list per root keyed by folder mtime (about 5-6 ms, re-list 0.37 ms on change); 2 option 1 plus defer stamp capture to first query (flat prepare, semantic change); 3 option 2 plus an FSEvents/inotify feed (only option flat in N for new sidechains).
